tier_reason: First-party vendor numbers (Cesanta sells Mongoose's commercial licence) against lwIP, seen only through WebSearch result summaries because mongoose.ws and eevblog.com are EGRESS_BLOCKED; no benchmark code, compiler, flags or HTTP workload is published in the repo, so it cannot reach A or B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (mongoose.ws and eevblog.com EGRESS_BLOCKED). Search-result summaries of an EEVblog forum post (thread 'ch32v307, risc-v minicore with ethernet', msg5177385, headed 'How does it compare to lwIP?') report HTTP throughput on a Nucleo-F746ZG with an Ethernet dongle of 1080 requests/s for Mongoose's built-in stack vs 286 requests/s for lwIP raw API and 16 requests/s for lwIP sockets (about 3.8x and 67x, derived from snippet data), with firmware about 28k for Mongoose vs 114k-160k for the lwIP variants (the summaries disagree on which lwIP variant is 160k). The benchmark_url article itself, per its search summaries, reports footprint and integration size only, no requests/s: flash 50,140 vs 67,020 bytes, RAM 22,524 vs 31,504 bytes, 3 vs 279 files and 32k vs 105k lines added, Ethernet driver 250 vs 3,300 lines (Mongoose vs lwIP).
corrections.caveats: First-party vendor measurement by Cesanta, which sells Mongoose's commercial licence. Every figure comes from machine-written WebSearch summaries: mongoose.ws (both lwIP-vs-Mongoose articles) and eevblog.com are EGRESS_BLOCKED here. The requests/s figures (1080 vs 286 vs 16) are not on the benchmark_url page according to its summaries; they come from an EEVblog forum post and possibly the 'lwIP vs Mongoose ... (Part 1)' article at mongoose.ws/articles/lwip-vs-mongoose, neither of which could be opened. The benchmark_url article measures footprint and integration effort, not speed, and one summary names its board as Nucleo-F756ZG rather than F746ZG. Compiler, flags, lwIP configuration (lwipopts.h buffer and window tuning), HTTP server used on top of lwIP, response size, keep-alive and client tool were not seen; 16 requests/s for lwIP sockets is far below typical lwIP results and suggests untuned defaults, so the gap may reflect configuration as much as stack design. The repo README links the integration article but has no numbers and no benchmark directory. Licence is GPL-2.0 (strong copyleft) or a paid commercial licence.

notes: Kept at C, snippet only: req/s claim (Mongoose 1080 vs lwIP raw 286 vs lwIP sockets 16 on Nucleo-F746ZG) traces to an EEVblog forum post and possibly mongoose.ws Part 1, not to the benchmark_url, which (per summaries) holds only flash/RAM/lines-of-code footprint numbers; all three pages are EGRESS_BLOCKED.
